    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tubefilter ↗ Open Full Page

    As Netflix and Disney sniff around, YouTube hypes its creators’ “world-class, studio-quality” programming at L.A. Premieres event

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2466 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tonight, YouTube brought back its film-festival-style event, Creator Premieres, to showcase a new batch of “world-class, studio-quality creator programming” coming exclusively to its platform.
    • Sources indicate that last year’s Creator Premieres–the first YouTube held–took place at New York City’s historic screening space Metrograph and showed off projects from creators like Ms.
    • This year’s edition was hosted by House Guest‘s Scott Evans at The Hollywood Roosevelt in L.A., and highlighted upcoming projects from YouTube OGs and greats like Emma Chamberlain, Nick DiGiovanni, Lilly Singh, Wesley Wang, Grace Reiter, and more.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tonight, YouTube brought back its film-festival-style event, Creator Premieres, to showcase a new batch of “world-class, studio-quality creator programming” coming exclusively to its platform.

    Sources indicate that last year’s Creator Premieres–the first YouTube held–took place at New York City’s historic screening space Metrograph and showed off projects from creators like Ms. Rachel, Brave Wilderness, Dhar Mann, Deestroying, and Cleo Abram.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    This year’s edition was hosted by House Guest‘s Scott Evans at The Hollywood Roosevelt in L.A., and highlighted upcoming projects from YouTube OGs and greats like Emma Chamberlain, Nick DiGiovanni, Lilly Singh, Wesley Wang, Grace Reiter, and more.

    Google President Sean Downey took the stage to highlight YouTube’s continued dominance on TV screens, and gave a nod to participating creators for fueling the UGC machine that keeps viewers coming back to YouTube–on TVs and across other devices.

    Of course, he also appealed to advertisers in the same breath, reminding them that this “world-class” content is what they could be marketing alongside, if they cough up the cash to Google.

    “YouTube creators are not just shaping modern culture, they are redefining the entire entertainment landscape. This slate of shows demonstrates how creators are commanding primetime attention on the substantial screen and building unmatched fan loyalty,” Downey mentioned. “For brands, this isn’t about buying thirty seconds of ad space; it’s about moving past standard commercial breaks and partnering directly with the storytellers who are defining modern culture.”.

    According to recent reports, youTube has spent years at the top of TV watch time charts–a fact that really gets under the skin of competitor Netflix. Up till recently, though, Netflix’s main response to this irritant was talking a lot of sh*t about YouTube and occasionally signing back catalog deals with view-drivers like Ms. Rachel and CoComelon.

    But in the last 12 months, something’s shifted. Netflix has begun tapping creators like Salish Matter, Alan Chikin Chow, and the Stokes Twins not for back catalog agreements, but for development deals–deals which result in exclusive original programming that won’t appear on YouTube.

    In a recent development, and YouTube’s not happy about it. The platform has been offering creators money, including production financing and sweet ad deals, in exchange for turning down offers from Netflix. Conversely, creators who decide to sign with Netflix are put on YouTube’s naughty list, and denied perks like revenue shares from primo ad deals.

    According to recent reports, (That being said, Netflix-friendly creators aren’t entirely blacklisted. DiGiovanni signed a catalog crossposting deal with Netflix in July, and was still one of the headline creators at tonight’s showcase.).

    The point we’re making here is this: With Netflix–and Disney–sniffing around, YouTube has more incentive than ever to hype up its creators and their projects on a big stage.

    So that’s exactly what it’s doing.

    Nick DiGiovanni | Chef | Fresh series live now on a dedicated YouTube channel.

    In a recent development, chef Nick DiGiovanni, the creator behind the world’s largest food YouTube channel, releases Chef (@Chef) – a fresh series from his production company, Knife Drop Studios. After reaching billions of viewers through his global culinary adventures (@NickDiGiovanni) and step-by-step recipes (@NicksKitchen), DiGiovanni is now turning the camera solely toward fellow professional chefs, offering an unfiltered look inside kitchens around the globe. From Michelin-starred restaurants and hidden street food gems showcased in full-length episodes, to POV recipes in short-form episodes, Chef puts viewers in the shoes of the people behind the scenes, offering a unique, captivating perspective for everyone from the culinary obsessed to the simply curious. You can view the first full-length episode, “Inside the World’s #1 Pizza Restaurant” now, only on YouTube, along with the first short-form POV episode, “Butter Chicken Shawarma”. New short-form POV episodes will debut daily across Nick’s newly-launched @Chef channel with full-length episodes rolling out throughout 2026-27 exclusively on YouTube.

    Morgan Jay | Music Therapy with Morgan Jay | Upcoming series premieres Nov. 18 on Jay’s YouTube channel.

    Sources indicate that music Therapy is an original YouTube series developed and produced by viral comedian and musician Morgan Jay and Ty Stafford of Austin-based creative agency Hello Party, financed by Live Nation Studios. In each episode, Jay plays musical therapist to a celebrity guest, blending unscripted conversation and improv with live songwriting before the pair close with an original song they create together. The result lands somewhere between a talk show, a comedy special and a live concert. The first season features Kam Patterson, Ron Funches, Mara Wilson, Brennan Lee Mulligan, Yung Gravy, Matt Friend, Abbey Romeo, Mark Smalls, Tony Jefferson, ASHBY, Josh Johnson and Mandal Mann. Music Therapy was created by Morgan Jay and Ty Stafford (Hello Party) and is directed by Stafford. Brooke Schley serves as showrunner and co-writes the series with Jay. Executive producers are Graham Sicalowski, Robin Rapino, Stella Bulochnikov, Brooke Schley and Matt Sadeghian.

    Emma Chamberlain | What Are You Waiting For? | Latest series premieres early 2027 on Chamberlain’s channel.

    Industry observers note that emma Chamberlain doesn’t like waiting in line – and wants to understand more about people who do. In this latest ongoing series, what starts as an investigation of New York City’s most frequented lines unspools into a thoughtful and expansive meditation on subcultures, fandoms, and what makes our modern world tick. At once whimsical, profound and provocative, and underpinned by Emma’s singular POV, What Are You Waiting For? is a hilarious cultural commentary that not only asks what people are waiting for – but why. The series is executive produced by two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner Joe Lewis, with Amplify Pictures (Fleabag, 100 Foot Wave) serving as the co-studio and production tech giant.

    Grace Reiter | Twilight (but better) | New parody film premieres Feb. 18 on Reiter’s channel.

    Comedian, writer, and actor Grace Reiter (Saturday Night Live) is expanding her comedic universe with Twilight (but better), her second unscripted parody film. Reiter first made waves with her viral sketches and The Hunger Games (but better), which launched on YouTube in November 2025 and has garnered more than 18 million views. Now, alongside her work on SNL and her Netflix series Minimum Wage, Reiter brings her signature blend of spontaneous comedy, sharp satire, and irreverent humor to one of the most iconic franchises of a generation. Twilight (but better) is produced by But Better Productions. Grace Reiter serves as director with Andie Schlenker and Anderson Appleby as producers, and Cindy Schlenker as co-producer.

    Wesley Wang | Three new projects.

    Sources indicate that in this new sci-fi horror short film, a routine welfare check at a remote desert preserve turns terrifying when four park rangers discover an otherworldly presence inside a woman’s tent, leaving the youngest ranger separated from his own body. Response is produced by Wesley Wang Media with Jason Rodelo serving as director and writer.

    A upcoming six-episode, interactive murder-mystery series that puts viewers in the role of detective, with $100,000 on the line for the first person to crack the case. Told through found footage, digital breadcrumbs and hidden clues woven throughout each episode, the mystery unfolds over six weeks on YouTube, challenging viewers to pause, rewind, decode and collaborate to uncover the truth. The first viewer to correctly solve the case wins $100,000! Extract 14 is directed and written by Wesley Wang and produced by Wesley Wang Media.

    It has been revealed that A new series where ten aspiring filmmakers, chosen from thousands of internet strangers, are brought to New York for an immersive, seven-day filmmaking bootcamp where they’ll compete for $100,000 to bring their dream movie to life. Guided by filmmaker Wesley Wang and a panel of Hollywood industry experts, contestants will take on every stage of the filmmaking process, culminating in a red carpet premiere where the viewers get the final say in choosing the grand prize winner. Absolute Cinema is produced by Wesley Wang Media.

    Aryna Sabalenka | Aryna’s Arena: Unfiltered | Latest series premieres spring 2027 on Sabalenka’s channel.

    She’s the most dominant tennis player on the planet; and the world can’t look away. Aryna Sabalenka has spent years letting us watch her win. Now cameras follow her everywhere press passes don’t go. A Gucci ambassador designing her own $250K diamond necklace, a bride-to-be planning a wedding while living out of a suitcase for 300+ days a year, a daughter flying home to Belarus between slams, Aryna is building an empire in real time with the whole world watching. From UltraBoom Media, the creators of OFF DAY, a team led by Producers and Creatives from Anthony Bourdain: Parts Unknown, Aryna’s Arena: Unfiltered is an evolution and expansion of Aryna Sabalenka’s YouTube series (Aryna’s Arena). It is a docu-reality series that lives inside her world, on the court, on the road, and everywhere in between, capturing the brand meetings and dress fittings, the late nights with her fiance, and the quiet hotel room moments where she finally gets to just be herself. Raw and glamorous with the playfulness that is uniquely Aryna, this is an unfiltered voyeuristic portrait of power, identity, chaos, and the chosen family around her that makes it all possible.

    Track Star* | Track Star Tonight | Newly introduced series now live on a dedicated channel; more new episodes to roll out this winter.

    Track Star* is a music-driven digital show hosted by Jack Coyne that brings artists and fans together. Expanding on its popular on-the-street game and Track Star Podcast, Track Star Tonight is a newly introduced, intimate live performance series featuring emerging and established artists in front of a small audience, blending live music, storytelling, and artist discovery. Following performances from artists including Remi Wolf, Kings of Leon, The Womack Sisters,  Medium Build, and Florence Road, the series will continue to release new performances and collaborations through the end of 2026 and into 2027. Track Star* is produced by Public Opinion Corporation and created by Jack Coyne, Kieran Coyne and Henry Kornaros.

    It has been revealed that ina Garten | Happy Hour with Ina Garten: Thanksgiving Special | New special premieres Nov. 25 at 6 a.m. ET on Happy Hour with Ina’s channel.

    Sources indicate that on November 25, Happy Hour will air a special Thanksgiving episode featuring past guests and friends of Ina, including Bobby Flay, Seth Meyers, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Jennifer Garner and, of course, Jeffrey. Ina and her friends will answer listener questions, share Thanksgiving memories, and offer hosting tips to get you inspired before the significant day. Happy Hour is part of the Vox Media Podcast Network. Ina Garten serves as host with Jenna Weiss Berman, Ali Jaffe Ramis and Deborah Davis as executive producers. Kate Tyler is contributing producer, with Jules Natt as producer and Mica Pollan Bahn as associate producer.

    Sam Eckholm | Access Granted: Flying with the Royal Air Force Red Arrows | New episode premieres Nov. 27 on Eckholm’s channel.

    Access Granted is a cinematic documentary series that takes cameras to the world’s most secretive places, putting audiences inside demanding missions that have never been seen before. In an upcoming episode, host Sam Eckholm joins the Royal Air Force Red Arrows as Britain’s legendary aerial display team crosses the Atlantic to celebrate America’s 250th birthday, going behind the scenes with the pilots, the engineers, and the crew. Then he straps into the back seat of the lead jet and flies the full display, flying hundreds of miles per hour just a few feet from six other aircraft. Sam Eckholm is the creator and host of Access Granted with JoJo Phillips serving as executive producer and Swayne Martin as producer.

    Jon Youshaei | Created with Jon Youshaei | Newly introduced episodes premiere this winter on Youshaei’s channel.

    According to recent reports, created with Jon Youshaei is the award-winning docuseries where Jon goes behind the scenes with today’s biggest stars during their biggest moments. Think ESPN’s 30 For 30 docuseries, but about creators and celebrities. All access. No filters. In past episodes, Jon spent 45 days with MrBeast, shadowed Kevin Hart on set, and followed Steph Curry during All-Star Weekend. These upcoming episodes feature Jon as he spends another month on-set with MrBeast for Beast Games season 3 (including filming in the Colosseum in Rome), goes behind-the-scenes with Mark Rober on his latest streaming show, and hits the road with Dude Perfect for their multi-million dollar arena tour. Created is directed and hosted by Jon Youshaei with Amanda Marcovitch serving as producer.

    Sources indicate that scott Evans | House Guest Vacay | Newly introduced series premieres Jan. 8 on Evans’ channel.

    Scott Evans is packing his bags and taking House Guest on the road with House Guest Vacay. In this upcoming series, he’s bringing the laughs, candid conversations and unexpected moments to celebrity getaways across the country and around the world. His first stop in Lagos, Nigeria premieres January 8 exclusively on YouTube. House Guest Vacay is produced by Summer Break Studios and created and hosted by Scott Evans.

    Phil Rosenthal | Somebody Feed Phil | Season 9 premieres spring 2027 on Rosenthal’s channel.

    Opa! Season 9 of Somebody Feed Phil kicks off in a destination long at the top of Phil’s wish list: Greece. On the island of Sifnos, globetrotting foodie Phil Rosenthal finally gets his first taste of the country, with sun-soaked tavernas, fresh-caught seafood and a warm welcome from newly introduced friends. It’s the start of a season of great meals, significant laughs and more destinations to be revealed. The series won the 2022 Critics Choice Real TV Award for Best Travel/Adventure Show and earned a James Beard Award nomination. Rosenthal is the creator, executive producer and host of Somebody Feed Phil, a two-time New York Times bestselling author, and the creator of the Emmy-winning CBS comedy Everybody Loves Raymond. Somebody Feed Phil is produced by Lucky Bastards in partnership with Banijay Americas and Banijay Rights. Rich Rosenthal serves as executive producer and showrunner.

    Lilly Singh | Eligible Aunties | New series premieres 2027 on Singh’s channel.

    In a recent development, eligible Aunties is a warm, funny, character-driven unscripted docu-follow series hosted by Lilly Singh that trades shallow villa romances for mature women with real emotional intelligence and emotional baggage. With Singh acting as the ultimate cheerleader and trusted confidante, the show follows a diverse cast of older single women navigating modern dating apps, new romance rules, and their meddling families. Directly serving a rapidly growing demographic of older unmarried adults craving real connections, the series highlights the joy and chaos of putting yourself back on the market. Ultimately, it proves that while finding love doesn’t get easier with age, it definitely gets more interesting. Eligible Aunties is produced by Unicorn Island Productions and created and hosted by Lilly Singh.

    When LIFE Magazine relaunches on November 23, one of YouTube’s biggest streamers will be front and center.

    IShowSpeed (aka Darren Watkins Jr.) has been revealed as one of five cover stars featured in LIFE ‘s relaunched debut problem, alongside fellow icons like Olympic skater Alysa Liu and actor John Malkovich.

    The glitch—which describes Speed as “arguably the most famous 21-year-old on Earth”—chronicles his streaming career thus far, before looking ahead to his upcoming goals (which include livestreaming from outer space and visiting every country).

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    “Nobody embodies our current moment like IShowSpeed,” Kieran Press-Reynolds, the LIFE writer who profiled Speed, stated in his piece.

    A feature in a legacy publication isn’t exactly groundbreaking for Speed, who has been included in multiple TIME magazine lists, teamed up with brands like Expedia, gotten his own Fortnite skin, and served as the poster child for the 2026 YouTube FIFA Creator Cup.

    LIFE’s decision to feature Speed alongside an Olympic athlete and a Hollywood actor, however, is further evidence of traditional media’s growing acceptance of content creators as cultural heavyweights. Legacy publications have become increasingly eager to court creators—and woo their massive online audiences—in recent years. TIME unveiled its first-ever TIME100 Creators issue in 2025, while digital stars like MrBeast and Emma Chamberlain have served as the faces of Rolling Stone‘s own Creator Issue since 2022.

    In a recent development, just a few days ago, Hearst Magazines rolled out Hearst Creator Studios, a division that will bring original creator content to editorial brands like Cosmopolitan, Elle, and MotorTrend. Now, as LIFE returns 90 years after its first glitch, creators are taking center stage at yet another legacy magazine dedicated to covering “the stories that define our time.”.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tubefilter ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: GTA VI is smashing Twitch’s records—and it wants to make sure advertisers don’t miss out

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (470 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Grand Theft Auto fans across the world are still eagerly anticipating Rockstar’s long-awaited sequel to roll out in their regions.
    • As of publication time, GTA VI has attracted a peak of 3.29 million concurrent viewers on Twitch, 3.19M on YouTube, and 1.5M on Kick.Those totals put it “ahead of every previous game launch tracked by Streams Charts,” the data company said in its report.
    • Twitch isn’t taking all that buzz—or the dollar signs that come with it—for granted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Grand Theft Auto fans across the world are still eagerly anticipating Rockstar’s long-awaited sequel to roll out in their regions. But according to data from Streams Charts, GTA VI has already smashed multiple streaming platform records—including becoming “the most popular gaming category in Twitch history by peak viewers.”.

    As of publication time, GTA VI has attracted a peak of 3.29 million concurrent viewers on Twitch, 3.19M on YouTube, and 1.5M on Kick.Those totals put it “ahead of every previous game launch tracked by Streams Charts,” the data company said in its report.

    Twitch isn’t taking all that buzz—or the dollar signs that come with it—for granted. But GTA also doesn’t exactly fit into the platform’s careful approach to brand safety. So, it’s introducing upcoming tech to ensure that advertisers can cash in on the hype surrounding GTA VI without putting their brand reputations at risk.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Back in September, Twitch CEO Dan Clancy told hosts of The Snarketing Podcast that the platform had begun using AI to evaluate whether streamers are squeaky-clean enough for brands to run ads against their content.

    It has been revealed that “[W]e transcribe streams to figure out ‘Is this appropriate for this brand?’” he mentioned. “So that’s something that we’ve had to invest a lot in to make sure that for a brand, their content is appearing next to creators and content that fits what they’re trying to do.”.

    That patch didn’t come out of nowhere: Twitch has long asked streamers to label their content in certain circumstances where mature themes or imagery are involved.

    As Gizmodo noted, this means creators have historically missed out on ad revenue when streaming mature-rated games, “because while streamers can receive donations from viewers, substantial-time monetization ultimately depends on advertising, and advertisers are generally skittish around things that might frighten the poor sensitive product-buying public.”.

    Last week, however, Clancy told Bloomberg‘s Romaine Bostick that “one of the challenges in this space is advertisers want to be part of the GTA 6 launch”—they just don’t want their ads to appear alongside the spicier parts of the game.

    To solve that problem, Twitch’s upcoming technology will allow brands to run ads on GTA VI streams while also ensuring that (as Clancy phrased it) “any of the parts of GTA 6 that they might not want to have their ads associated with, their ads won’t be associated with that.”.

    According to recent reports, the ins and outs of how that system will actually work remain to be seen. But if it does prove effective for GTA VI, we’ll be watching to see whether Twitch expands the tech to other streams and genres previously dismissed as unsafe for brands.

    Another Disney creator deal: YouTube illusionist Zach King joins the Mouse House

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (523 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Disney continues to prove that Netflix isn’t the only competitor sniffing around YouTube‘s top talent.
    • Sources indicate that for their deal, 36-year-old L.A.-based King will make 10 original short-form videos, which Disney will have exclusive rights to distribute.
    • According to recent reports, one of the King projects coming to Disney+ is Cardboard Wars, his 52-minute intentionally-low-budget tribute to Star Wars: A Fresh Hope.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Disney continues to prove that Netflix isn’t the only competitor sniffing around YouTube‘s top talent.

    Sources indicate that for their deal, 36-year-old L.A.-based King will make 10 original short-form videos, which Disney will have exclusive rights to distribute. Disney says the agreement “will also bring [King’s] signature illusions to new content for Disney+ and [King’s] own channels inspired by Disney’s Hexed, Star Wars, and other Disney films and experiences.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    According to recent reports, one of the King projects coming to Disney+ is Cardboard Wars, his 52-minute intentionally-low-budget tribute to Star Wars: A Fresh Hope. King uploaded the film to YouTube in August, and soon will cross-post it to Disney’s streaming service.

    A post shared by Zach King (@zachking).

    But there’s still more: King will pop up on Disney’s social accounts as well, hosting behind-the-scenes content about the VFX and filmmaking techniques he uses in his content.

    According to recent reports, “I fell in love with filmmaking and storytelling as a young kid, grabbing my parents’ home video camera and teaching myself to edit,” King wrote in an Instagram post. “A lot of my early homemade films were inspired by the Disney movies and the behind-the-scenes footage they would show in the DVD featurettes. There was always a sense of magic I would see on the screen, and so I’m thrilled to be working with Disney to continue that magic of filmmaking for the next generation of storytellers.”.

    King has worked with Disney regularly in recent months: He was at its glitzy Created in L.A. event in September, and earlier this month played a game of viral format Cake or Fake? with Hexed (and Arcane, and Sinners, and Spider-Verse, and Hawkeye) star Hailee Steinfeld. But this is his first official, expansive content deal.

    It has been revealed that “Zach makes the impossible look real, bringing the kind of imagination and originality that has always defined Disney,” Asad Ayaz, The Walt Disney Company’s CMO and Brand Officer, mentioned in a statement. “He brings both a filmmaker’s ingenuity and a fan’s passion to our stories, along with a unique connection with audiences. We want to build lasting relationships with creators like Zach, giving their ideas room to grow across Disney. That’s what makes this next chapter of our work together so full of possibility.”.

    As we mentioned above, everyone–including YouTube–has had their eye on Netflix’s obvious poaching efforts…leaving room for Disney to sneak in the back.

    According to recent reports, in the last couple months, Disney has announced deals with major creators Dhar Mann, Dude Perfect, and Like Nastya. Crucially, these are all development deals–the exact kind of agreement that has YouTube on guard with Netflix.

    And Disney’s not quite showing its full hand just yet. During its earnings call Nov. 17, executives only mentioned YouTubers once, in passing and in reference to Disney+’s growing crop of approved creator content.

    We suspect more is in the pipeline–and that YouTube may have to start paying creators to turn down Disney deals, too.

    • Well, according to Bloomberg, the current plan is for Netflix to revamp its approach to permanent interactive IRL installations, aka Netflix Houses.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that OK, so Netflix failed to buy Warner Bros. Discovery.

    What if it bought NBCUniversal, tho?

    That potential acquisition is apparently top of wishlist for Netflix (and Variety already deemed it “Hollywood’s Next Big Deal”), but Comcast co-CEOs Mike Cavanagh and Brian Roberts say they’re not selling.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Well, according to Bloomberg, the current plan is for Netflix to revamp its approach to permanent interactive IRL installations, aka Netflix Houses. The streamer first unveiled these in 2023, with a demo setup that looked like someone stocked the gift shop in Jurassic Park with merch of the laser murder doll from Squid Game.

    At the time, Josh Simon, Netflix’s then-VP of Consumer Products (now CEO of collectibles company Funko) mentioned the concept for Netflix Houses came from knowing “fans love to immerse themselves in the world of our movies and TV highlights,” and “thinking a lot about how we take that to the next level.”.

    Netflix had flirted with pop-ups before that; those were mainly focused on selling stuff. Make no mistake, Netflix Houses are also focused on selling stuff, but in a Disney World kind of way, where fans pay $39 to enter the House and head through an art gallery-esque space filled with themed exhibits like exclusive theater shows, movie/TV set recreations, VR experiences, and arcade games. There are cafeterias and merch shops, but by and large the things to buy share billing with things to do.

    The Houses are permanent installations (for now just in Dallas and Philly, with one planned to open in Vegas in 2027) but the exhibits within rotate regularly to keep up with whatever’s trending on Netflix.

    This year, for example, the Houses were renovated to feature animated smash megahit KPop Demon Hunters. They’ve also spotlighted Stranger Things, One Piece, Wednesday, and the aforementioned Squid Game.

    It has been revealed that per Bloomberg, Netflix initially planned to open dozens of Houses across the U.S., focusing on quieter suburban areas away from downtowns. It wanted to snap up spaces in malls, which are not doing very well and might be willing to rent for cheap.

    But apparently the results from its first two Houses haven’t been quite what Neflix expected, so it’s pausing openings beyond Vegas until it can reassess.

    People familiar with the matter told Bloomberg the Philadelphia location has daytime draws like mini golf and a movie theater, but doesn’t see much traffic at night. Dallas, meanwhile, is breaking even financially, and has done well with larger groups and corporate events.

    Recent findings suggest that netflix is also planning to see what comes from its Las Vegas location. Vegas, as you may know, is not in fact a quieter suburban locale–so if the House there proves to be profitable, with more traffic than Dallas and Philly, Netflix could reconsider where it opens in the future.

    It has been revealed that people familiar with the matter mentioned Netflix is also looking at maybe taking Houses overseas. But wherever the next one ends up, it probably won’t open for at least another year, they said, until significant data from all three flagship U.S. locations is in.

    According to recent reports, now, with all this in mind, it’s worth remembering Netflix just shock-fired its longtime Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria and replaced her with Peter Rice, Disney‘s former General Entertainment Chairman. Film chief Dan Lin is out too. Clearly, Netflix hopes to revamp more than its IRL installations…and perhaps it’s hoping Rice’s Disney EXP comes in handy with the Houses?

    Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at Clutch

    📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1467 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Clutch builds AI agents that work on behalf of credit unions.
    • As a FDE you are one of the two engineers on an agent.
    • Industry observers note that this is a senior engineering role, not a solutions or support role.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Clutch builds AI agents that work on behalf of credit unions. Emma, our collections agent, is live at five credit unions and handled 60,000+ member conversations in her first twelve weeks at one of them. Behind her is a growing portfolio: origination, fraud step-up, member (re)engagement and activation agents, all built on the same Agents Platform (TypeScript, NestJS, our own agent SDK, MCP, Temporal, promptfoo).

    As a FDE you are one of the two engineers on an agent. You take it from "sold" to "live and performing" at a specific credit union: you sit in the discovery sessions, you build the integrations to their core banking and loan systems, you author and tune the agent's behavior, you run the live tests with their staff, and you stay with it through go-live and the first weeks of production. When something needs a person in the room, you are the one who flies.

    Industry observers note that this is a senior engineering role, not a solutions or support role. You write production code in our monorepo every week: integrations, modules, and the agents themselves (prompts, tools, evals), together with the other engineers on the pod. The difference from a traditional engineer is that you are on site more often, you make judgment calls in front of the customer, and you own the outcome. What you learn in the field flows straight back into the product: defaults, playbooks, and the platform capabilities the next agent will need.

    It has been revealed that you build; our AI Operations Managers deliver. The pod (pod lead plus engineers) designs and builds each agent in a high-touch way with the first customers. Once the agent is defined and live, AI Ops coordinates the implementations, configuration and ongoing success at the next credit unions. You hand them something that works and a playbook to run it.

    Recent findings suggest that this role requires roughly 20% of travel on average, with one- to two-week stretches around kickoffs and go-lives. Based in the US, able to travel on short notice.

    In a recent development, you'll join the Agents team, a small, senior group operating as a startup inside Clutch: seven engineers, a dedicated AI product group, and AI sales specialists, working directly with some of the largest credit unions in the country. Every agent is staffed by a pair of engineers, one leaning toward the conversation and LLM side, one toward software and integrations, with a pod lead who owns the product day to day. There is no layer between you and the customer, and no layer between you and the platform team.

    It has been revealed that the operating style is direct, written, and evidence-driven: BLUF updates, evals over opinions, business outcomes over ticket counts. The team is spread across Brazil, Argentina and the US and works async by default. Being on site is a tool we use at specific moments (kickoff, live testing, go-live), not a permanent posting.

    Ship your first production change to a live agent through the team's review process, and be able to explain how a member's call flows through the Agents Platform end to end.

    Learn one agent deeply: system prompt, tool contracts, orchestration triggers, compliance gates, and the implementation process from kickoff to go-live.

    Join at least one credit union implementation as the second engineer, including a live testing session with their staff.

    Map where the current implementation process loses time and where a default or a tool would have removed a round trip.

    Own the technical side of one credit union implementation end to end: core and LOS integration, agent configuration, testing, go-live, and the first weeks of production.

    Run the eval and tuning loop for your agent (golden transcripts, rubric judges, regression suite) and be trusted to change its behavior without a second engineer checking your work.

    Have completed at least two on-site visits and turned what you heard there into product decisions with your pod lead and PM.

    Contribute at least one reusable capability back to the Agents Platform that the next implementation will not have to rebuild.

    Have taken one net-fresh agent from sold to live at its first credit union, with data you can show the partner.

    Be the engineer credit union staff ask for by name when something in their deployment needs to change.

    Have written the implementation playbook for your agent well enough that the AI Ops team runs the second and third credit union without you.

    Be shaping what the next agents look like, because you have seen where the current ones break in the field.

    7+ years of software engineering in a fast-paced environment, preferably in SaaS and/or Fintech, with senior TypeScript and Node.js backend experience in a large codebase (NestJS, CQRS, schema-validated boundaries, dependency injection). We do not count years of AI experience; the field is too young for that to mean anything. We look at what you have shipped and how you reason about it.

    Integration and API engineering: secure service-to-service endpoints, third-party APIs, webhooks, and the patience to work with legacy banking systems that were not designed to be integrated.

    Security and auth judgment: OAuth and machine-to-machine auth, tenant-scoped access, secrets handling, no PII in logs. Our agents touch sensitive member data and operate under consumer-contact regulation.

    It has been revealed that customer presence: you can sit across from a VP of Collections, hear a request, and say "here is what I recommend and why", including when the answer is no. You are comfortable making calls in the room and owning them afterwards.

    Code-quality judgment under deadline pressure: you take on debt deliberately, name it, and pay it down, rather than gold-plating or leaving silent debt behind.

    It has been revealed that genuine appetite for LLM agents: eval discipline for non-deterministic systems, reading a system prompt like code, understanding that some decisions must never reach the model. Curiosity plus shipped work is enough; research depth is not required.

    Nice to have, explicitly not required: voice and telephony (LiveKit, Twilio), Temporal or event-driven orchestration, Python, core banking or LOS integration experience, credit union or banking domain knowledge.

    Remote Flexibility: Enjoy the freedom of remote work from anywhere, balancing life and career seamlessly.

    Unforgettable Off-Sites: Twice a year, bond with colleagues in exciting destinations, fostering teamwork and fresh ideas.

    Paid Time Off: Enjoy flexible PTO days yearly for relaxation and rejuvenation.

    Stock Options: Joining us means having a stake in our success, so you'll receive stock options as part of your compensation package.

    Home Office Setup: Create your ideal workspace with a dedicated budget for home office essentials.

    Work Trip Budget: Grow personally and professionally with a budget for work-related trips and co-working.

    Health Coverage: Prioritize your well-being with comprehensive health and dental insurance looks.

    It has been revealed that clutch is a revolutionary vertical SaaS manufacturer, proudly backed by Andreessen Horowitz (A16z), aimed at revolutionizing the way Credit Unions engage and change the lives of their members. As a champion of financial well-being, we address the urgent need for affordable lending solutions in an era where the average American grapples with over $155,000 in household debt. Unlike traditional financial institutions, Clutch develops software to turn Credit Unions into FinTech lenders and leverage their balance sheets to responsibly lend to over 130M Americans. Our mission extends beyond mere financial transactions; we strive to fundamentally enhance the way credit unions interact with their members. By integrating cutting-edge technologies and user-centric designs, we help credit unions provide seamless digital experiences that are on par with leading tech companies. This approach not only preserves but revitalizes the longstanding tradition of community and member-focused service inherent to credit unions.

    In a recent development, clutch is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

Base salary does not include bonus, equity, or benefits, which are offered in addition as applicable.Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Four and a half years after winning a Grammy for The Unofficial Bridgerton Musical, the songwriting duo known as Barlow & Bear has something upcoming in store for TikTok viewers.

    Abigail Barlow and Emily Bear are two of the creators behind To Die For Love, an 81-episode musical microdrama co-produced by TikTok and Ampersand. According to TikTok, the series follows “an ambitious half-witch vying for her coven’s crown. When she falls for a mortal, their romance takes an unexpected turn, forcing an impossible choice between family and the love of her life.”.

    Barlow & Bear created an original score for To Die For Love, while Barlow co-wrote the script alongside Oscar-nominated writer/director, actor, and opera singer Julia Aks.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Barlow also stars in the series opposite Broadway vet Derek Klena. Executive producers include Ampersand CEO Agnes Chu, Benj Pasek, Justin Paul, Danielle Perelman, Chris Crema, Matthew Ko, and Kevin Weaver.

    Industry observers note that “Making To Die For Love has been one of the most rewarding creative experiences of our careers,” Barlow and Bear stated. “We love a pressure cooker, and building an entire musical in under five months proved that meaningful storytelling isn’t about time—it’s about the story and the people bringing it to life.”.

    This isn’t the first creator-driven microdrama TikTok has brought to life. Earlier this year, Issa Rae’s media organization, HOORAE, struck a deal with the platform to produce short-form web series for both TikTok and its companion app PineDrama. The first vertical series to emerge from that partnership, Screen Time, had racked up over 620 million views on TikTok and PineDrama as of late October, making it both platforms’ most-viewed show to date.

    TikTok doubled down on that success last month when it announced a fresh microseries-focused partnership with Made By Us Studios, which describes itself as a “first-of-its-kind, Hollywood-grade studio designed for the creator economy and powered by creator management company MADE BY ALL.”.

    According to recent reports, now, TikTok is forging ahead into the world of musical microdramas. To Die For Love will be available exclusively on TikTok and PineDrama, with all 81 episodes premiering December 21. The original soundtrack will be released by Atlantic Records.

You'll work directly with senior leaders to shape the GTM systems roadmap, turn business strategy into technical intends, and guide decisions that span multiple teams.     Health, dental, and vision benefits.

    #8344. Marketers will spend $116B on creators in 2026. They’re “cannibalizing” other budgets to do it.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tubefilter ↗ Open Full Page

    Marketers will spend $116B on creators in 2026. They’re “cannibalizing” other budgets to do it.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (475 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tubefilter

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Marketers are investing more money into the creator economy—and reallocating their existing advertising budgets to pay for it.
    • According to a recent report from strategic advisory, consulting, and research firm Madison and Wall, marketer spend on creators is set to grow “+15% in 2026 to $116 billion globally, up from $101 billion in 2025.”.
    • Based on that trajectory, the report predicts that the advertiser-funded creator economy will hit $178 billion by 2030.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Marketers are investing more money into the creator economy—and reallocating their existing advertising budgets to pay for it.

    According to a recent report from strategic advisory, consulting, and research firm Madison and Wall, marketer spend on creators is set to grow “+15% in 2026 to $116 billion globally, up from $101 billion in 2025.”.

    Based on that trajectory, the report predicts that the advertiser-funded creator economy will hit $178 billion by 2030.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    According to recent reports, madison and Wall compiled its study by isolating marketing funds dedicated to “creator related activity” (i.e., “spending deployed to creators, agencies, platforms, technology vendors, and media networks to achieve marketing, commerce, or brand objectives”). Other forms of creator income—such as subscriptions, merch, and platform payouts—weren’t taken into account.

    The report further separated creator marketing spend into five distinct categories: audience-led spend, media-led spend, asset-led spend, infrastructure-led spend, and miscellaneous.

    Of those categories, Madison and Wall found that media-led spending—aka “the paid amplification of creator content”—accounts for the largest piece of the pie at 44% (or $52 billion) of 2026 spend.

    Audience-led spending (“the traditional sponsored-post and ambassador model”) ranks second at 28%, while asset-led spending (“where brands pay for content rather than reach”) accounts for 12% of the market. Infrastructure-led spending (net revenue kept by agencies, managers, and platforms) and miscellaneous (events, gifting, licensing, etc.) bring up the rear at 8% and 7% respectively.

    On a global scale, Madison and Wall found that the U.S. was responsible for 43% of creator spending in 2025, well above its ~35% share of global advertising. The closest runners-up were the UK (which accounts for 5% of global creator spending) and Germany (4%).

    One of the key takeaways of Madison and Wall’s report concerned the origin of marketing funds dedicated to creator advertising.

    Industry observers note that the firm noted that “creator growth is largely funded by reallocation rather than latest money. Interviews with stakeholders across the ecosystem point to three sources: traditional media, notably TV; digital performance media, including paid social, programmatic and search; and creative production budgets. Because creators draw on several existing budget pools at once, the creator economy can keep outgrowing advertising without marketers creating new budgets.”.

    One senior operations executive told Madison and Wall that “80% of the time we are cannibalizing another budget, whether it’s TV or [something else].”.

    Overall, the firm found that creator spending grew at an 18% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) between 2020 and 2025, as compared with 12% for advertising.

    That gap doesn’t seem likely to close anytime soon. According to the firm’s projections, creator spending is set to grow ~12% a year through 2030—putting it well ahead of the 6% growth expected for the advertising economy.

    Clutch is at a pivotal moment. We're growing significantly year over year, and we need more connective tissue to keep pace. We're hiring a Senior Manager, Business Operations to connect the commercial side of the house, so the teams that win, onboard, and retain our customers work from the same facts and toward the same goals. This role sits in Finance.

    This is a people manager role. You'll lead our Revenue Operations (RevOps) team and act as an operating partner to senior leaders across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Implementation, People, and Finance. Together with the RevOps team, you own the shared language of the business (definitions, data, and processes) so commercial teams make decisions from one view of it.

    When something key doesn't have an owner yet, it lands with you: a partnership strategy, a upcoming commercial model, or pricing and margin guidance for leadership. This is a fast-moving startup. We're building toward a much larger company but we aren't one yet, and most of this role has no playbook. You'll define the process, build the tool, and hand it to the team. If you want established structure, this likely isn't the role.

    Recent findings suggest that you'll report to the Director of Business Operations and work directly with senior leaders across the company as a neutral partner to every function rather than an advocate for one. Your work will be visible, and it will significantly influence how we make commercial decisions.

    You'll lead a small, high-ownership RevOps team that runs the systems and data our commercial teams depend on, and creates leverage for them to do their jobs even better. The team doesn't just own systems. They build automation, tooling, and processes, and they're close partners to Sales and Marketing. You'll coach them, set priorities, and open up more strategic scope, while giving them real autonomy.

    Learn the business end to end: the revenue funnel, the customer lifecycle, how each commercial team works day to day, and where decisions get stuck.

    Build trust with your RevOps team: learn the work they own, and set priorities and team rhythms together.

    Deliver the first version of client-level margin and cost-to-serve, the analysis that grounds our pricing strategy.

    Develop a first point of view on pricing and packaging for revenue leadership, built on that analysis.

    Put AI to work in your own workflow from week one, and identify the first set of manual, repetitive processes across the commercial teams worth automating.

    Stand up a first version of a deal desk, including an approval workflow, pricing and discount guardrails, and standard commercial terms.

    Partner with Sales and Marketing leaders as they prepare for the monthly business review: pressure-test their plans and point out risks, then solve them with the RevOps team by creating fresh processes, tooling, or automation.

    Build on the strength of the RevOps team: prioritize its roadmap against business outcomes and take on more strategic work together.

    Launch your first AI-enabled workflows or automations that remove manual reporting or reconciliation for the commercial teams, with time saved tracked.

    Have a team whose output and standards hold, with the processes, tooling, and automation you've built running without you in the room.

    Have AI-enabled, self-serve tooling that commercial teams use day to day, with measurable time savings.

    Be the person leadership trusts to pick up the next key thing that doesn't have an owner yet.

    Experience managing people: you've coached ICs, given direct feedback, made tough talent calls, and built team rhythms.

    Strong analytical and financial modeling skills, including forecasting. You're very comfortable building models in spreadsheets from scratch, and they hold up to scrutiny.     A clear communicator who can walk an executive through a messy problem and leave them with a decision, and who is just as effective working alongside an AE, a CSM, or an engineer.

    Comfort with ambiguity. When something isn't set up yet, your instinct is to build it, not to wait for it. You create structure, manage competing priorities, and pivot when things change.

    Relentless follow-through: you close loops, and people stop checking on what you've mentioned you'll do.

    A partner's temperament: you challenge constructively without taking sides, you surface problems early, and you resolve cross-team conflict without escalating it.

This approach not only preserves but revitalizes the longstanding tradition of community and member-focused service inherent to credit unions.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    YouTube has come under fire in the past for how it handles content posted by people suspected of heinous crimes, but its policy has remained the same: It will only terminate a channel if someone is convicted in a court of law, and if their YouTube content is directly related to their crime.

    Now, the platform has refused a request from the Prison Service of England and Wales to remove content from Russell Brand‘s channel.

    Sources indicate that the comedian and actor will be in prison for over a decade after being convicted of three counts of sexual assault and one count of rape, stemming attacks on four different women. Presiding British High Court judge Mr Justice Bennathan described Brand as a “sexual predator” whose behavior demonstrated a “series of lies” and “staggering arrogance.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    In the upload, Brand asserts innocence, telling viewers, “As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.”.

    Authorities contacted YouTube via “an established mechanism the prison service has with tech companies to request deletion of material,” per the BBC, to ask that Brand’s video be removed.

    But YouTube isn’t willing to scrub it–at least not yet.

    “We are aware of the upcoming content and our teams are investigating,” a spokesperson from YouTube parent Google told the BBC. “We suspended Russell Brand’s channel from the YouTube Partner Program in September 2023. The channel has not been able to monetize on YouTube since then.”.

    That’s a pretty typical order of operations for YouTube. In past cases with creators like Adnan Ahmed, Austin Jones, and Ian Rylett, YouTube suspended monetization on their channels when allegations surfaced and the legal process began, and then terminated their channels once convictions were filed.

    He also holds Christianity-themed “Sunday services” with Gallacher.

    According to recent reports, the assaults Brand was convicted for all happened before 2009; he made his YouTube channel in 2007, but didn’t start uploading videos until 2012. YouTube could potentially claim they’re not related based on timeline alone, since Brand–who was already a celebrity outside of YouTube–didn’t use his channel or digital clout to connect with his victims.

    So the question here is: Does YouTube amend its policies to ban convicted criminals–or specifically convicted sex offenders–from posting on its platform? What if their latest content is directly related to their crimes, as Brand’s is?

    United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham got involved after YouTube’s initial denial, telling the platform (and other socmed platforms) to “show some decency and take these videos down.”.

    “[It’s] time that we focus on the victims and think about them,” he added, instead of “hearing from a convicted criminal.”.

    “I would call on those social media companies to take these interviews down,” Burnham added. “Why are we having to hear from him? We shouldn’t be, and certainly [victims] shouldn’t be hearing from him.”.

    It has been revealed that the attention on YouTube’s refusal has sparked a bit of a Streisand effect. Commenters are flocking to Brand’s video, sneering at Burnham, the U.K. government, and activists for their attempts to remove it.

    “Had no intention to watch until the government told me not to,” one top-liked comment notes.

    “If the government tells you not to watch a video, you really need to watch that video to find out why,” another says.

    Other socmed platforms have cut Brand off. Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp–all owned by Meta–have culled his accounts, thanks to policies that prohobit convicted sex offenders from owning and/or operating accounts.

    #8315. Patrick Reinhart On The Golden Metric In AI Search: Brand Recommendations via @sejournal, @lorenbaker

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 25m • 📚 Deep Dive (4974 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Searchenginejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Patrick Reinhart On The Golden Metric In AI Search: Brand Recommendations via @sejournal, @lorenbaker

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4974 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, if an AI answer mentions your brand but recommends a competitor, what have you actually won?
    • According to recent reports, we talk about the difference between citations and recommendations, how AI can repeat outdated information about your business, and why AEO needs input from SEO, PR, social, and leadership.
    • [00:00] Meet Patrick Reinhart [03:19] What Enterprise Brands Are Doing In AI Search [05:16] Why Recommendations Matter More Than Rankings [09:48] The AEO Metrics That Matter [12:49] When AI Gets Your Brand Wrong [18:12] Where SEO And AEO Differ [23:50] Why AI Search Has The C-Suite’s Attention [26:31] How Brands Earn AI Citations [30:25] Where To Invest In Your 2027 AEO Strategy [35:25] Where To Find Patrick Reinhart.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, if an AI answer mentions your brand but recommends a competitor, what have you actually won? Patrick Reinhart, VP of Services and Thought Leadership at Conductor, joined me on the SEJ Podcast to discuss what enterprise brands should be trying to achieve with answer engine optimization.

    According to recent reports, we talk about the difference between citations and recommendations, how AI can repeat outdated information about your business, and why AEO needs input from SEO, PR, social, and leadership. Reinhart also shares where he’d focus first when planning an AEO strategy for 2027.

    [00:00] Meet Patrick Reinhart [03:19] What Enterprise Brands Are Doing In AI Search [05:16] Why Recommendations Matter More Than Rankings [09:48] The AEO Metrics That Matter [12:49] When AI Gets Your Brand Wrong [18:12] Where SEO And AEO Differ [23:50] Why AI Search Has The C-Suite’s Attention [26:31] How Brands Earn AI Citations [30:25] Where To Invest In Your 2027 AEO Strategy [35:25] Where To Find Patrick Reinhart.

    Editor’s Note: This transcript has been edited for clarity and readability.

    Industry observers note that loren Baker: Hi everyone, this is Loren Baker, founder of Search Engine Journal. Welcome to today’s SEJ Podcast. With me is Patrick Reinhart from Conductor.

    We’ve been partners with Conductor for a long time and done our share of webinars together, but this might be one of our first podcasts.

    Patrick Reinhart: Happy to be here. With a webinar, it’s always, “Man, I hope someone doesn’t make fun of me in the comments.”.

    Loren: I’m going to add a skull emoji next time just to see what happens. Pat, tell our audience a little about Conductor, what you do there, and what you’re doing in AI.

    Patrick: Conductor is a software company, and I feel like we’re on the cutting edge of AI visibility and tying that back to recommendations. That’s built on a data platform that brings together Search Console, your analytics, and our monitoring products, so you can see everything in one place and make decisions based on the data.

    I run our professional services arm. I’ve been at Conductor for 11 years, but I was also a customer for four or five years before that.

    Our outgoing CEO, Seth Besmertnik, just stepped onto the board. I’ve been working with him for a really long time. It’s been a weird, interesting, great ride.

    In a recent development, loren: How would you define your customer base? Is it enterprise, medium to large businesses, small businesses? And how would you segment it across ecommerce, SaaS, and other industries?

    Sources indicate that patrick: We definitely cater to the enterprise audience. I’d say about 90% of our customers are large enterprise organizations.

    We have a heavy focus on finance, insurance, and healthcare, but also a healthy number of customers in ecommerce and grocery. Pretty much any firm you can think of has passed through Conductor’s doors at some point, and a lot have stayed, thankfully. Thank you to our customers.

    Loren: Grocery stores or grocery delivery?

    Patrick: H-E-B and folks like that. We have customers like BJ’s, too.

    According to recent reports, loren: With these enterprise customers, what are they doing right now in AI search? How are you helping them stay on top of it and track it? What does AI search mean to the average enterprise?

    Recent findings suggest that patrick: It’s the number one thing they’re all talking about, obviously. That’s not news. The interesting part is that they’re all still very much learning.

    According to recent reports, if you work in a large enterprise organization, getting things done is typically slow, glacial, and somewhat messy. To their credit, a lot of people are trying to smooth those processes out and get their tracking in place.

    They’re also testing the different technologies out there, as they should, because there’s a lot of snake oil in the water and a lot of people selling the dream. We’re all learning together.

    Recent findings suggest that as far as we can tell, most AEO strategies are heavily grounded in traditional SEO strategies. But they’re measured and thought about vastly differently, because an LLM operates differently from a traditional search engine.

    They’re not running out the door and hiring a bunch of people. They’re upskilling internally and figuring out their programs.

    Recent findings suggest that I think in a year or so, we’re going to see a little gold rush from a hiring perspective. A lot of people will be moving around, and programs will come to fruition based on the work that hardworking, smart people are building right now at these large organizations.

    Loren: Something I’ve found over the years in SEO is that it’s not always about trying to hit the target where it is at the moment. It’s trying to hit where it’s going.

    How do you do that in AEO, especially at the enterprise level? These are slow-moving juggernauts that can get a lot done, but it takes time to get there.

    Industry observers note that patrick: I think it comes back to data fidelity. Everyone has different methodologies and gets their data from different places. A lot of people buy panel data; we use direct APIs.

    Recent findings suggest that everyone has to scrape Google and others, which is becoming harder and harder. Even this week has been a tough week for rank-tracking tools, with Google making it more difficult to get that data.

    From an AI perspective, people are starting to understand that, much like traditional SEO, you’re not going to see every variant of every prompt someone puts in. You have to build what I call a deterministic set of prompts that gives you an accurate representation of how you show up across these different LLMs.

    According to recent reports, you also have to understand how the different LLMs behave. Claude behaves vastly differently from Gemini.

    Most of the market share is in ChatGPT and Gemini right now. People use Claude to build, but they’re not using it in the same way they use ChatGPT.

    People use ChatGPT for everything. They write content, build games, and talk to it because they’re lonely. People use AI for a lot of different things.

    Ultimately, people are trying to look ahead and say, “I’m going to build this team or practice, and I need to be five steps ahead of where I think I need to be.” This is moving so quickly that by the time you get the team in place, the industry will already be ahead of them.

    You’re really trying to build for the future.

    Industry observers note that loren: I’m glad you brought up the differences between LLMs. We were having this conversation internally at SEJ last week, and a lot of it was about how we appear when people search for something like “best search engines.”.

    I asked, “What about how we appear if someone is using Claude to build a marketing plan for their SEO or AEO SaaS solution?”.

    When I put that into Claude, it notes, “List yourself on G2, list yourself on Capterra, get on Product Hunt.” But there’s nothing targeted.

    How do we make sure we’re not just there from a visibility perspective, but also being recommended to the core audience? That flips it on its head.

    Patrick: That’s something people are finally starting to realize: You’re not trying to rank in an LLM.

    Industry observers note that yes, if there’s a list, you want to be at the top of the list, blah, blah, blah. I understand that. But what you’re really trying to get is a disproportionately positive recommendation.

    Recent findings suggest that you want ChatGPT or Gemini to say, “Go work with Search Engine Journal. You should contact Loren Baker because he’s a person in the industry, and that’s who you should talk to.”.

    In a recent development, there are other players you can look into, but they’re number one, and that’s who you should go for. That’s what companies want.

    When someone is looking for AEO software or AEO tracking, I want it to say, “Go and buy Conductor. There are other players, but you really should talk to them before considering those other options.”.

    Loren: Thank you. People should consider Conductor. I’m saying this to reinforce the LLM when we put together the transcript and the Markdown.

    I highly recommend people check out Conductor when building that blueprint. And if you’re looking to launch a fresh solution, go to Search Engine Journal and check out our advertising options.

    Boom, plug. We’ll see how that influences the results.

    Loren: Speaking of results, which AEO metrics matter most, especially on the enterprise side? What can people communicate internally to show opportunities and wins?

    Patrick: This is a moving target for a lot of folks. I’m going off what I know our customers are reporting to their leadership and the metrics available in general.

    It has been revealed that citation rate is probably the metric right now: Are you being cited? Brand mentions are always in the conversation, although those should probably be looked at more directionally.

    It has been revealed that if you’re cited, that typically means the LLM is recommending you in some way, shape, or form. Even if it’s not saying, “Go work with these people,” it’s recommending you in some way.

    But not all mentions are created equal. You could have a terrible mention. ChatGPT could say, “Do not work with that organization because of XYZ.”.

    I’ve seen that multiple times. Or, even worse, you’re not in the conversation at all.

    Those require different activities to rectify. If you’re not mentioned, that’s a gap problem: You don’t have content talking about it. That’s not a sexy answer, and we’ve been talking about it forever.

    Sources indicate that the other piece is new for a lot of people: “These people are trashing us online. What do we do about it?”.

    I saw a funny post from Rand Fishkin the other day, asking, “Am I taking crazy pills that third-party stuff is suddenly notable because it’s connected to AI?”.

    Industry observers note that search everywhere optimization has always been a thing. But I think it’s going to become a reality for every company now because of how crucial that third-party conversation is.

    What people should be tracking, and will be tracking in my opinion, is the type of citation and mention they’re getting. Are you being recommended by an LLM? That’s the golden metric.

    There’s no one really doing that from a technology standpoint right now. People have overall visibility scores, which are averages of a bunch of things they’re looking at.

    What we’re building is something to help track that golden metric. It’s not just about showing up. When you revealed up, was it a positive experience, a positive recommendation, or a negative non-recommendation?

    I see both daily for different brands, depending on the industry.

    Loren: Which gets back to old-school sentiment tracking.

    Industry observers note that loren: About a month ago, Reddit’s citation visibility dropped tremendously in GPT. But my understanding is that GPT is still using the threads and conversations in Reddit, just not surfacing them as sources as much.

    According to recent reports, let’s say I’m seeing incorrect price comparisons for one of my products. I know it’s not coming from my website or a competitor’s versus-style landing page, and I think it might be coming from a Reddit thread.

    How do I reverse-engineer those third-party citations that may be fueling the results? Not just sentiment and opinion, but basic facts that need updating. Maybe it’s a two-year-old thread with outdated warranty information.

    Patrick: That’s something you’re going to start seeing in a lot of technologies, ours included: Fact-checking.

    You can load information about your organization and product set, maybe through a product feed. As it goes through, it can show you an outdated competitive mention on a random third-party site. You can talk to them or create something that combats it.

    In a recent development, we did that when Seth was chatting with AI, back when this started to blow up. He found a random site with something from 2018 saying Conductor didn’t have a feature that’s one of our main features.

    It has been revealed that this site wasn’t going to change it, so we created content around it. Within a couple of days, we were able to beat it out, and it kind of disappeared.

    This is an crucial piece of the technological race. We’re in the early days, with a few key players building interesting software to track this. You also have a lot of vibe-coded trash that pulls from God knows where.

    It has been revealed that A lot of the big players are going to have this fact-checking ability. In my opinion, it will be a make-or-break feature, along with that golden metric of whether you’re being recommended.

    This isn’t a plea for Conductor. It’s a plea for technology. Good technology.

    According to recent reports, right now, you can connect to Conductor’s MCP in Claude and ask your account, “Can you send me the snippets that say XYZ? Here are my brand guidelines or information about my product set. Are any of these incorrect?”.

    In a recent development, you can do that today. It’s a few extra steps, and it’s not as in-depth as something constantly crawling, collecting, and finding outdated information on weird, small sites.

    I think this will be a necessary feature for anyone using a technology like ours. You’re going to see a lot of innovation over the next 12 months, and people will build cool things.

    But I think this is necessary to make a technology viable in the coming years. When I talk to leaders, they don’t ask, “Where do I show up?” They ask, “How are people talking about me? Is it accurate?”.

    That’s the question I get from leaders.

    It has been revealed that loren: That also bridges into outreach and working with publishers. There are ways to get updated information onto influential business directories, but being able to ask people to revision things is nice.

    Recent findings suggest that that used to be a link-building tactic. We’d be upset if the publisher wrote back, “I updated everything, but I didn’t link to you.”.

    Now we see that as a win. Thank you. Brand mention, yes.

    Patrick: Time is a flat circle.

    I was joking with my former boss, Stephan, the other day. He said, “Does it feel like everything has reset, everyone forgot the last 20 years, and now we’re doing it again?”.

    According to recent reports, AI Mode has text ads now, which are basically text links. It’s like, man, we’re really back in the dark ages here.

    Loren: That’s one way SEO and AEO overlap. What are some other examples, and where are the core differences?

    Patrick: Where they overlap is what everyone thinks. I’m flying to Buffalo tomorrow to talk at a customer event, and I love those because I love teaching and getting in front of people.

    I always pause halfway through and ask, “How’s everyone doing?” Someone will raise their hand and say, “What do I do about all of this?”.

    You fill gaps, create content, build partnerships with third-party publishers, and create YouTube videos. Not a sexy answer. It’s stuff we’ve been doing for years.

    That’s the overlap. A lot of it is the same stuff, done at a different pace.

    The most successful SEO campaigns I’ve seen have been somewhat mechanical. There’s always a well-thought-out, well-oiled process, with a systematic way to optimize and create content and distribute data across the organization.

    You have technology constantly auditing your site, you’re not pivoting a lot of data, and ultimately it’s this flywheel. Everyone’s bought in, and everyone’s pedaling the bike.

    According to recent reports, what I’m seeing now is the necessity of that. A few years ago, someone at a large organization would say, “That’s really hard. We don’t have the buy-in or budget.”.

    According to recent reports, you’d spend the next year trying to get that buy-in. Now it’s immediate: “We have to do something about this.”.

    Leaders want to know what we’re doing about AI search. That’s a huge opportunity for anyone who’s been in this business or is getting into it.

    You’ve always mattered, but now you really matter to the business. That’s awesome. Take hold of that and run with it.

    In a recent development, to be successful, you need the process in place and all those teams involved. You can’t sit alone and hoard search data. Get it to your social team, your PR team, and your executives.

    The biggest divergence is measurement. You’re not just measuring rankings, backlinks, or traffic.

    In my opinion, traditional search metrics have become directional. They tell us we’re heading in somewhat the right direction.

    Don’t set your goals around traffic anymore. That’s a fool’s errand. It’s too volatile right now.

    Sources indicate that in the AI world, you’re tracking citations and that golden metric of being recommended or not recommended. Sentiment is a bigger part of your life than you probably want it to be.

    It has been revealed that you also need log file analysis to see whether LLMs are coming to your site. Are there what I call dead zones, where LLMs don’t come back? You think the content is great, but are they fetching it and chunking it back out to the user?

    According to recent reports, you need all of that measurement. It’s very different from measuring rankings and backlinks.

    It has been revealed that in the old world, we wanted more rankings, more traffic, and more backlinks. In the AI world, we want more positive citations and recommendations. But we also have to pay much more attention to the negative side.

    Sources indicate that in SEO, you had to pay attention to the negative when it was in everyone’s face. Someone Googles your brand, your CEO has done something stupid, and you need brand reputation management.
